title: menuz: a macOS menu bar app whose menu is a YAML file of commands to run
objective:
A new utility, `menuz`, that puts a menu of hv's own commands in the macOS menu bar. The menu is entirely a YAML file in a menuz config directory: the file says what the menu holds, each item runs something (a script, a `utilz` verb, any shell line), an item that needs parameters acquires them from the user before it runs, and whatever a run prints goes to one known `menuz.log` that can be tailed. The app reads its whole menu from the config files, notices when they change and updates the menu, and realises the variables in the menu each time the menu is displayed. The first thing on the menu is `arngz`: apply a desk from the menu bar.

Three working menu bar apps already exist in sibling projects (Intent.app, Conflab.app, Gtools.app), all one shape: an xcodegen project, an `AppDelegate` with an `NSStatusItem`, the login shell's `PATH` handed to every child, `SMAppService` for launch at login, Apple Development signing, build products off the tree, and an `install` verb that builds Release, replaces the bundle under `~/Applications` and launches it with launchd's environment. menuz is that shape cut to a menu read from a file, and it invents nothing the shell or macOS already does: variable interpolation is the login shell's own expansion, parameters are acquired through macOS's standard dialogs, the log is a file `tail -f` reads.

v1 is: the app (the menu from the file, watched, realised at open; parameters; the runner; the log and the notice), and the `utilz menuz` shim with `init`, `edit`, `log`, `validate`, `render`, `build`, `test`, `install`, `uninstall`, `start`, `stop`, `restart`, `status`, `stamps` and `doctor`.
context:
Asked by hv on 16 Oct 2026, directly to vc, just before a compact: "a very simple macOS (Swift) menu bar app that is entirely customisable from a yaml file that points to a .menuz config directory (in the appropriate location for that kind of dir) ... The main use case for menuz is for me to be able to run a list of common utilities easily by just selecting them from the menubar. The obvious one that I want to try is arngz." hv asked for the write-up first and a rubber-duck session to refine it before any code, and added two standing instructions on the bounce: the three sibling menu bar apps (`../Intent`, `../Conflab`, `../Gtools`) are the pattern, "we DO NOT need to reinvent the wheel here"; and nothing is rebuilt that macOS or the standard unix utilities already do, interpolation included.

The thread is created and started ahead of the rubber-duck: design.md carries the shape, the questions hv left open with vc's recommendation on each, and the work packages. The design's open questions are settled with hv before WP-02 starts; WP-01 is that settlement. Doc before code holds: no source under opt/menuz until the design stands.

wps.title: Design settled with hv
wps.body:
## Decisions

hv ruled on 16 Oct 2026 in vc's session, the rubber-duck of WP-01. In hv's words where hv gave them.

| D   | Decision                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| --- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| D1  | As recommended: the config directory is `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/menuz/`, `MENUZ_HOME` overriding.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| D2  | As recommended: Yams parses the yaml in the app, Codable models, one parser.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| D3  | As recommended: interpolation is the login shell's own expansion of labels and `each` lines, one `zsh -ilc` per menu open, asynchronous, the last values shown first, capped. No menuz syntax.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| D4  | hv: "One form with all params, typed (where possible)." One window per run holding every param, each field typed from the param's declaration where the yaml gives a type (string, number, path, choice, bool), free text otherwise. Not the standard dialogs.                                                                                                                                                                   |
| D5  | As recommended: `menuz.log` under XDG state, `utilz menuz log` tails it, a notification on a non-zero exit, `notify:` per item.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| D6  | hv, first to vc: "It's built here locally for dev in native/macos like the other menbar apps, and the installed into opt. There should be a 'use dev\|opt' option like the way devbin has that feature." Then, in cc's session, hv asked where Intent.app, Conflab.app and Gtools.app live, "we should be consistent", and picked the siblings' target (confirmed to vc: "See the utilz-cc correction on install location"). So: the source and the xcodegen project at `native/macos/Menuz/`; the dev build under `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/menuz/build/macos/Build/Products/<Config>/`, as Intent's and Gtools' do; the installed copy at `~/Applications/Menuz.app`, Gtools' and Conflab's target (Intent's signed release goes to /Applications); a `use dev\|installed` switch, after devbin's own, says which the shim's launch and status use. |
| D7  | hv: "Same as Intent. This is opensource just like Intent and it needs to be signed properly." Developer ID, notarised, shipped as a release asset the keg installs; not the Apple Development model.                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| D8  | As recommended: the menu bar glyph is an SF Symbol named in the yaml, `terminal` by default; no asset pipeline. (hv's "8: Left running" is read as Q9, since "left running" is Q9's alternative; hv is told so.)                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| D9  | hv: "Left running, surely?" Runs in flight at Quit are left running, detached from the app (their own session, stdin from /dev/null, stdout and stderr on the log file directly rather than through the app), so the app's exit closes nothing they write to. The log records the quit and names the runs still going.                                                                                                             |
| D10 | hv: "Yep": `each` is in v1.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| D11 | hv: "Yep, agree": `Menuz.app`, `com.matthewsinclair.utilz.menuz`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

criteria.text: design.md records hv's ruling on each of its questions Q1 to Q11 as a numbered decision or a descoping, in hv's words where hv gave them, and no recommendation is left standing in its place.

state.evidence: hv's rulings of 16 Oct 2026 on Q1 to Q11, recorded as D1 to D11 in WP-01's body (and in design.md's Decisions section at the 0605 sync): Q4 one typed form, Q6 the source and dev build at native/macos/Menuz with the installed copy at ~/Applications/Menuz.app like the siblings and a use dev|installed switch (hv's correction in cc's session, confirmed to vc), Q7 Intent's signing, Q9 runs left running, Q10 and Q11 yes, the rest as recommended; no recommendation left standing in a ruling's place

criteria.text: The example menuz.yaml in design.md is final, its params typed as D4 rules, and is the one menuz init writes; swift is a declared language of the project (intent lang init swift) and critic-swift is the review for native/macos/Menuz.

utilz menuz is dispatched by bin/utilz; opt/menuz/menuz.yaml declares the utility with opt/menuz/VERSION as the one home of its version; utilz list shows menuz; utilz doctor reports xcodegen and xcodebuild only when native/macos/Menuz is present, as it reports cargo only when a crate is.

init creates MENUZ_HOME (default ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/menuz) with the example menuz.yaml and an empty bin/, refuses to overwrite an existing menuz.yaml without --force (exit 2, naming the file), and a second run changes nothing; edit opens the yaml with open -t, or $VISUAL/$EDITOR under --editor; log prints the log's path then tails it, -n N prints the last N lines; each refuses by name, exit 2, when its file is missing.

validate and render run the app's --validate and --render arms on menuz.yaml or a given file and pass their output and exit code through, proven with a fake Menuz binary on PATH; with no app built or installed they refuse by name, exit 2; status reports installed (~/Applications/Menuz.app), running, login item, source-current and which build use selects (dev or installed), without Xcode present.

The app is an xcodegen project at native/macos/Menuz in the siblings' shape (Swift 6, macOS 14, LSUIElement, the test-host guard; signed and notarised with Developer ID on release as Intent's is, D7) with Yams as its one package; --validate and --render run without a menu bar and exit 0 or 2 with every finding named, and --version prints the stamped version.

The menu is exactly the file, in order: items, captions, headers, separators, submenus, then the fixed tail (Edit Menu, Open Log, Reload, Quit menuz); every validation rule in the design refuses its fixture naming file, entry path, key and value, and the example passes; a file that fails keeps the last good menu and shows the refusal as a disabled first item and in the log.
Hand run on hv's machine, recorded as such: a save of menuz.yaml, an atomic rename by an editor, and a deletion and recreation of MENUZ_HOME each reach the menu within one second with no restart.

Labels and each lines with a $ or a backtick are realised by the login shell at every menu open in one zsh -ilc invocation, asynchronously, the last values shown first and titles updated in place, under the realise cap with the previous value kept and the overrun logged; a label with neither is never sent to the shell; each expands to one item per stdout line with MENUZ_ITEM set.

An item's params are acquired through one form window holding every param in order (D4), each field typed from the param's declaration (string, number, path, choice, bool; secret hidden) with its prompt and default; Cancel runs nothing and logs cancelled; required refuses an empty answer and a typed field refuses a value of the wrong type, each named in the form; the values reach the run as exported variables under the declared names.

Each run is /bin/zsh -ilc of the run line, with the login shell's PATH and MENUZ_HOME/bin first on it, cwd the item's, else the file's, else HOME, stdin /dev/null, and MENUZ_HOME, MENUZ_LABEL, MENUZ_RUN_ID and (under each) MENUZ_ITEM exported; runs are concurrent, each with its own id, detached from the app (their own session, stdout and stderr on the log file directly, not through the app); Quit leaves runs in flight running and logs each as left running with its id (D9).

Every run appends to ${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/menuz/menuz.log, created on first use: a start line (timestamp, run id, item, cwd, the run line as written), stdout and stderr lines as they come prefixed with the run id, and an end line with exit code and duration; a secret's value never appears; a line the app cannot write is an error in OSLog and a notification.

A run that exits non-zero posts a notification naming the item and the exit code; notify: always posts one on every finish carrying the last output line; notify: never posts none; the item's notify overrides the file's.
Hand run on hv's machine, recorded as such: the example menu applies an arngz desk chosen from the each-generated items, and discover saves one through a text dialog, with both runs in the log.

build runs xcodegen only when project.yml or the set of sources changed and xcodebuild Debug or --release with products under ${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/menuz/build/macos as Intent's and Gtools' do; test runs the MenuzTests target; install builds Release, quits every running copy, replaces ~/Applications/Menuz.app (the siblings' target, D6), unclaims the build products, registers the bundle and launches it with an empty environment; use dev|installed records which build the shim's launch and status use, after devbin's own switch; uninstall, start, stop, restart and stamps as designed; each refuses by name, exit 2, without xcodegen or xcodebuild, and install refuses when native/macos/Menuz is absent.
Hand run on hv's machine, recorded as such: the app registers itself as a login item on its first run, status reports it, and the menu is back after a logout and login.

CI: a macOS job on a tag builds the app, signs it with Developer ID, notarises it and attaches it as the release asset, as Intent's does (D7); on dispatch it builds unsigned and runs MenuzTests; the Linux legs run menuz.bats with the fake app in the explicit utility loop; both green on the closing SHA.

help/menuz.md, the README's menuz section and the CHANGELOG entry exist and name every verb and flag the CLI accepts, checked against menuz --help; bin/devbin check all and the estate suite are green; the hand-run transcript in acceptance.md names the machine, the macOS build and the Xcode version.
